targets.claim: USCIS will continue processing work permits for migrants even if the federal government shuts down.
USCIS has taken steps to expedite the work permit application process, including offering education sessions.

claims.quote: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) will continue processing work permits for migrants even if the federal government shuts down.
claims.reason: The evidence explicitly states that USCIS will continue its work even if the federal government shuts down, funded by filing fees.
claims.evidence_quote: Even if the federal government shuts down this weekend, the federal agency in charge of handling work permits and other applications from asylum seekers will continue its work.

claims.quote: The agency has taken steps to expedite the process, including offering education sessions, issuing alerts, and providing mobile biometric services.
claims.reason: The evidence confirms all three measures: education sessions at libraries, email/SMS alerts, and mobile biometric services including fingerprinting.
claims.evidence_quote: the organization has taken steps to speed up the work permit application process, is providing education sessions for immigrants at libraries, and has issued email and SMS alerts to migrants about their eligibility for work permission. Additionally, the organization provides mobile biometric services including fingerprinting.

claims.quote: additional funding from Congress is needed to process more applications
claims.reason: The evidence confirms Jaddou stated Congress should give the organization more funding to process more work permits and TPS applications.
claims.evidence_quote: Jaddou claimed Congress should give the organization more funding so it can process more work permits and TPS applications.
